parts.prompt_html: Carry out an appropriate test at the 5% significance level of the claim that the population mean exceeds 250.5 g. State your hypotheses and give a conclusion in context.
parts.answer_html: \(t=1.973\) with \(\nu=8\). There is sufficient evidence at the 5% level that the population mean exceeds 250.5 g.
parts.solution_html:
Let \(\mu\) denote the relevant population mean.

\[H_0:\mu=250.5,\qquad H_1:\mu>250.5.\]

Using the unbiased variance estimate,

\[\bar{x}=\frac{2264.3}{9}=251.588889,\]
\[s^2=\frac{\sum x^2-(\sum x)^2/9}{8}=\frac{21.9288889}{8}=2.74111111.\]
\[\mathrm{SE}=\frac{s}{\sqrt{9}}=0.551876708.\]

Under \(H_0\), the test statistic has a \(t_{8}\) distribution.

\[t=\frac{\text{sample estimate}-\text{null value}}{\mathrm{SE}}=\frac{251.58889-(250.5)}{0.55187671}=1.973.\]

The 5% one-sided rejection region is \(t\ge 1.860\).

Since \(1.973\ge 1.860\), reject \(H_0\). There is sufficient evidence at the 5% level that the population mean exceeds 250.5 g.

A random sample of 9 independent observations is taken from a normal population with unknown variance. A 95% confidence interval for its mean is reported as \([2.71,3.09]\).

This interval was calculated using the tabulated critical value \(t=2.306\). Treat the endpoints and this tabulated value as exact when reversing the calculation.

An independent sample of 11 segments from algorithm B gives

\[\sum y=34.32,\qquad\sum y^2=107.5624.\]

Both duration distributions are normal with the same unknown variance. Let \(\mu_A,\mu_B\) denote their population means.

parts.prompt_html: For the sample used to construct the stated confidence interval, recover \(\sum x\) and \(\sum x^2\) for this sample.
parts.answer_html: \[\sum x=26.1,\qquad\sum x^2=76.17878863.\]
parts.solution_html:
The interval is symmetric about the sample mean, and its half-width is \(h\).

\[\bar{x}=\frac{2.71+3.09}{2}=2.9,\qquad h=\frac{3.09-2.71}{2}=0.19.\]
\[h=t\frac{s}{\sqrt n}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad s^2=n\left(\frac{h}{t}\right)^2=9\left(\frac{0.19}{2.306}\right)^2=0.06109857839.\]
\[\sum x=n\bar{x}=26.1,\]
\[\sum x^2=(n-1)s_x^2+n\bar{x}^2=76.17878863.\]
parts.hint_html: Use the interval midpoint and half-width. In the variance formula, distinguish \(\sum x^2\) from \(\sum(x-\bar x)^2\).

criteria.criterion_html: Invert the interval to obtain the variance.

parts.prompt_html: Carry out an appropriate test at the 5% significance level of the claim that algorithm B has a greater population mean segment duration than algorithm A. State your hypotheses and give a conclusion in context.
parts.answer_html: \(t=2.105\) with \(\nu=18\). There is sufficient evidence at the 5% level that algorithm B has a greater population mean segment duration than algorithm A.
parts.solution_html:
Let \(\mu_B-\mu_A\) denote the relevant population mean difference.

\[H_0:\mu_B-\mu_A=0,\qquad H_1:\mu_B-\mu_A>0.\]

Using the unbiased variance estimate,

\[\bar{x}=\frac{26.1}{9}=2.9,\]
\[s^2=\frac{\sum x^2-(\sum x)^2/9}{8}=\frac{0.488788627}{8}=0.0610985784.\]

Using the unbiased variance estimate,

\[\bar{y}=\frac{34.32}{11}=3.12,\]
\[s_y^2=\frac{\sum y^2-(\sum y)^2/11}{10}=\frac{0.484}{10}=0.0484.\]
\[s_p^2=\frac{(8)s_x^2+(10)s_y^2}{18}=\frac{0.488788627+0.484}{18}=0.0540438126.\]
\[\mathrm{SE}=\sqrt{s_p^2\left(\frac1{9}+\frac1{11}\right)}=0.104488956,\qquad\nu=18.\]
\[\bar y-\bar x=0.22.\]

Under \(H_0\), the test statistic has a \(t_{18}\) distribution.

\[t=\frac{\text{sample estimate}-\text{null value}}{\mathrm{SE}}=\frac{0.22-(0)}{0.10448896}=2.105.\]

The 5% one-sided rejection region is \(t\ge 1.734\).

Since \(2.105\ge 1.734\), reject \(H_0\). There is sufficient evidence at the 5% level that algorithm B has a greater population mean segment duration than algorithm A.

The time to carry out a routine check is measured in minutes at two sites. Two independent random samples are taken: 40 observations from population A and 60 from population B. The observations are denoted by x and y, respectively.

Population A sample

\[\sum x=254,\qquad\sum x^2=1678.81.\]

Population B sample

\[\sum y=367.2,\qquad\sum y^2=2380.014.\]

The population variances are finite and need not be equal. Use a large-sample normal approximation.

Write \(\mu_A\) and \(\mu_B\) for the two population means, in the stated units.

parts.prompt_html: Find a 90% confidence interval for \(\mu_A-\mu_B\), giving both endpoints to 3 decimal places.
parts.solution_html:
Using the unbiased variance estimate,

\[\bar{x}=\frac{254}{40}=6.35,\]
\[s^2=\frac{\sum x^2-(\sum x)^2/40}{39}=\frac{65.91}{39}=1.69.\]

Using the unbiased variance estimate,

\[\bar{y}=\frac{367.2}{60}=6.12,\]
\[s_y^2=\frac{\sum y^2-(\sum y)^2/60}{59}=\frac{132.75}{59}=2.25.\]

The samples are large and independent. Use the normal approximation to the difference of sample means, with separate variance estimates; do not pool.

\[\mathrm{SE}=\sqrt{\frac{s_x^2}{40}+\frac{s_y^2}{60}}=0.282400425.\]

Use an equal-tailed 90% confidence interval for \(\mu_A-\mu_B\).

\[z_{0.95}\approx 1.645,\qquad\text{interval}=\text{estimate}\pm c\,\mathrm{SE}.\]
\[0.23\pm 1.644854\times 0.28240042=0.23\pm 0.46450736.\]

The interval is \((-0.235,\ 0.695)\) minutes.

This interval uses the large-sample normal approximation, with separate estimates of the two population variances.
parts.hint_html: A two-sided confidence interval leaves half of the excluded probability in each tail.

owner.stem_html:
The lengths of two types of component are measured in centimetres. Two independent random samples are taken: 10 observations from population A and 12 from population B. The observations are denoted by x and y, respectively.

Population A sample

\[\bar{x}=35.4,\qquad s_x^2=4.41.\]

The variance estimate uses denominator \(9\).

Population B sample

\[\sum y=409.2,\qquad\sum y^2=13989.36.\]

Assume that both populations are normal with the same unknown variance.

Write \(\mu_A\) and \(\mu_B\) for the two population means, in the stated units.

parts.prompt_html: Find a 95% confidence interval for \(\mu_A-\mu_B\), giving both endpoints to 3 decimal places.
parts.solution_html:
Using the unbiased variance estimate,

\[\bar{x}=\frac{354}{10}=35.4,\]
\[s^2=\frac{\sum x^2-(\sum x)^2/10}{9}=\frac{39.69}{9}=4.41.\]

Using the unbiased variance estimate,

\[\bar{y}=\frac{409.2}{12}=34.1,\]
\[s_y^2=\frac{\sum y^2-(\sum y)^2/12}{11}=\frac{35.64}{11}=3.24.\]
\[s_p^2=\frac{(9)s_x^2+(11)s_y^2}{20}=\frac{39.69+35.64}{20}=3.7665.\]
\[\mathrm{SE}=\sqrt{s_p^2\left(\frac1{10}+\frac1{12}\right)}=0.830978339,\qquad\nu=20.\]

Use an equal-tailed 95% confidence interval for \(\mu_A-\mu_B\).

\[t_{20,0.975}\approx 2.086,\qquad\text{interval}=\text{estimate}\pm c\,\mathrm{SE}.\]
\[1.3\pm 2.085963\times 0.83097834=1.3\pm 1.7333904.\]

The interval is \((-0.433,\ 3.033)\) cm.

The population variance is unknown: using a standard normal critical value instead of the \(t\) critical value would not be the specified small-sample procedure.
